WITH months AS (
  SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic,
         CASE WHEN booked_on >= '2025-12-01' THEN 'This month' ELSE 'Last month' END AS period,

ORDER BY topic, period

plan.question: Spending of 2025 on the account 'Sparkasse Stuttgart Gemeinschaftskonto', added up over the months, one row per month, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and cumulative_eur.

sql:
WITH per AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0 AND account = 'Sparkasse Stuttgart Gemeinschaftskonto'
  GROUP BY month)
SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(eur) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM per
ORDER BY month
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
'add up' is a running total, which is an area over the periods
it names one of the two accounts, so only the joint one counts
the columns are month and cumulative_eur
the period is the whole year 2025
reasoning_code:
the shape is area, so areaY draws the band and lineY its edge
the columns are month and cumulative_eur, and cumulative_eur holds the numbers
months on x with monthShort, euros on y
an area rests on zero, so its euro axis is the bare scaleLinear factory

request: Welchen Anteil an allen Abgaengen 2025 hat jedes unserer beiden Konten?

plan.title: Abgaenge je Konto
plan.question: Alle Abgaenge 2025 je Konto, eine Zeile je Konto, Spalten account und total_eur.

sql:
SELECT account, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
GROUP BY account
ORDER BY total_eur DESC

das Ganze sind alle Abgaenge, die Stuecke sind die beiden Konten
zwei Stuecke, also keine Restzeile
die Spalten sind account und total_eur

the shape is doughnut, so pie allocates the slices and radialArc draws them
the columns are account and total_eur, and total_eur is the value pie reads
the slices are the series, so color and key both name account
a doughnut has no axes, so scales.x and scales.y are null and the legend is on

request: Show me month by month what we spent at REWE.

plan.title: REWE per month
plan.question: Spending at REWE per month of 2025 over both accounts, one row per month, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and total_eur.

sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND coalesce(title, counterparty, description) = 'REWE'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month

a line reads a trend most directly
it names no account, so both of them count
the columns are month and total_eur

the columns are month and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
months on x with monthShort, euros on y

request: Bei welchen acht Empfaengern ging 2025 ueber beide Konten das meiste Geld raus?

plan.title: Die acht groessten Empfaenger
plan.question: Die acht Zahlungsempfaenger mit den groessten Ausgaben 2025 ueber beide Konten, absteigend, eine Zeile je Empfaenger, Spalten merchant und total_eur.

sql:
SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
GROUP BY merchant
ORDER BY total_eur DESC
LIMIT 8

liegende Balken tragen die langen Empfaengernamen als Beschriftung
sie sagt 'ueber beide Konten', also wird nicht nach Konto gefiltert
die Spalten sind merchant und total_eur
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_horizontal, so the mark is barX and nothing else
the columns are merchant and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
barX draws sideways, so the euro column is x and the names are y
scales.x is the euro axis and scales.y the band of names, none dropped

request: Show me per quarter of 2025 how my four smallest categories stack up.

plan.title: The four smallest categories per quarter
plan.question: Spending per quarter of 2025 for the four smallest categories of the year, one row per quarter and category, columns quarter as '2025-Q1', topic and total_eur.

sql:
WITH small AS (
  SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0
  GROUP BY topic
  ORDER BY SUM(-amount) ASC
  LIMIT 4)
SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND coalesce(category, 'Needs review') IN (SELECT topic FROM small)
GROUP BY quarter, topic
ORDER BY quarter, topic
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
four categories over four quarters, two dimensions that cross
'stack up' means the total per quarter matters, so stacked bars
it asks for the smallest four, so the ranking runs the other way round
the columns are quarter, topic and total_eur
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_stacked, so barY carries a series and no layout
the columns are quarter, topic and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
topic is the series, so it is the z and the color channel and it needs a legend
a quarter reads 2025-Q1, which is a name and not a month, so no monthShort and no label dropped

request: Stell November und Dezember 2025 fuer unsere fuenf groessten Kategorien nebeneinander.

plan.title: November neben Dezember
plan.question: Ausgaben im November 2025 und im Dezember 2025 je Kategorie, eine Zeile je Kategorie und Monat, der Monat heisst 'November' oder 'Dezember', die fuenf groessten Kategorien ueber beide Monate, Spalten topic, period und total_eur.

sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic,
         CASE WHEN booked_on < '2025-12-01' THEN 'November' ELSE 'Dezember' END AS period,
         -amount AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on >= '2025-11-01' AND booked_on < '2026-01-01'),
big AS (SELECT topic FROM months GROUP BY topic ORDER BY SUM(eur) DESC LIMIT 5)
SELECT topic, period, ROUND(SUM(eur), 2) AS total_eur
FROM months
WHERE topic IN (SELECT topic FROM big)
GROUP BY topic, period
ORDER BY topic, period
reasoning_plan:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
zwei Monate werden verglichen und nach Kategorie aufgeteilt, zwei Dimensionen, die sich kreuzen
gruppierte Balken stellen November neben Dezember je Kategorie
der Monat ist die Serie, die Kategorie die Position, also kommen die Zeilen lang
die Spalten sind topic, period und total_eur
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_grouped, so barY carries a series and layout: group()
the columns are topic, period and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
period is the series, so it is the z and the color channel and it needs a legend
category names on x on a band scale, none dropped and tilted, euros on y from the bare factory

request: Compare how the spending on the joint account and on the personal one add up over 2025.

plan.title: Joint against personal, adding up
plan.question: Spending of 2025 added up over the months inside each account, one row per month and account, columns month as 'YYYY-MM', account and cumulative_eur.

sql:
WITH per AS (
  SELECT account, strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0
  GROUP BY account, month)
SELECT month, account, ROUND(SUM(eur) OVER (PARTITION BY account ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM per
ORDER BY account, month
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
'add up' is a running total, which is an area, and 'compare' is a second one beside it
the account is the series, so one band per account and a legend
the two bands are read off the gap between them, so both start at zero
the columns are month, account and cumulative_eur
reasoning_code:
the shape is area and these rows carry a series, so one areaY and one lineY over all of them
the columns are month, account and cumulative_eur, and cumulative_eur holds the numbers
account names the series, so z and color on both marks and the legend goes on
the two bands are compared and not added, so each rests on zero: y1 zero, y2 the figure
an area rests on zero, so its euro axis is the bare scaleLinear factory
